name: RSHash
workload: Streaming and single k-mer lookup/build over large k-mer sets (genome datasets from Pibiri 2022), comparing a rank/select-bitvector hash construction against SSHash's PTHash-based dictionary.
claimed_speedup: RSHash is on average 1.4x and up to 2x faster than SSHash5 in streaming lookups (4.5x more k-mers/sec on average, up to 8.5x vs published SSHash3); ~0.5 microsecond/k-mer single lookup (fast variant), ~0.6 microsecond/k-mer (compact variant); 50% faster negative lookups; built 60% faster than SSHash using 40% less memory (verbatim from paper)
hardware: AMD EPYC 9454 @ 2.75 GHz, 1 TB RAM, single core, Debian (kernel 6.1.0-43), 64-bit
tradeoffs: Uses succinct rank/select bitvectors rather than a classical MPHF construction, so it is a competing technique in the same k-mer-dictionary space rather than an MPHF library itself; specialized to DNA k-mers, not general-purpose keys; very new/low-adoption project.
caveats: Baseline is another k-mer dictionary (SSHash) rather than std::unordered_map/CMPH/BBHash directly, so this is indirect (comparative) evidence for the category, included per orchestrator's genomics-blog guidance; project is very new (created Feb 2026) with only 8 stars.
found_via: Blogs / talks: found while following the k-mer MPHF blog trail from Camille Marchet's page and the SSHash lineage of papers; confirmed via the peer-reviewed RSHash paper (Bioinformatics 2026) and its GitHub repo/README.

verification.tier_reason: This tier covers only the off-category comparison against SSHash. The Bioinformatics 2026 paper (btag440, Sec. 5.3-5.6, Tables 4-6) states an AMD EPYC 9454 CPU and GCC 12.2 in release mode. The flags (-O3 -march=native) are in source/CMakeLists.txt. The benchmark code is public (benchmarks/benchmark_rshash.sh plus the rshash bench/locate commands), and the SSHash side is pinned to commits 5a13d6a and e65dcb2.
verification.notes: All claimed numbers match the PMC page. The rejection is on category scope only. Under a k-mer-dictionary category with SSHash as baseline, this would be a valid Tier A entry. Repo metadata checked: MIT license, not a fork, not archived, 8 stars, last commit on main 2026-07-31 (active).
verification.reject_reason: other: RSHash is a k-mer dictionary built on rank/select bitvectors and does not use an MPHF. Its only benchmark is against the SSHash k-mer dictionary (SSHash3 and SSHash5). There is no published comparison against std::unordered_map, CMPH, BBHash or any standalone MPHF, so it does not fit minimal-perfect-hash-functions.

name: SSHash
workload: Exact membership/lookup queries over billions of DNA k-mers (human and bacterial pangenome datasets) using an MPHF (PTHash) plus minimizer-based bucketing, benchmarked single-threaded.
claimed_speedup: 990 ns/k-mer positive lookup, 854 ns/k-mer negative lookup on the human dataset (canonical SSHash); 9.39 bits/k-mer space; 16.2 min / 17.3 GB peak memory to construct on the human dataset (derived from page data: paper Tables 4/5/7)
hardware: Intel Core i9-9940X (single core used for benchmarks), Ubuntu 19.10, Linux kernel 5.3.0, 64-bit
tradeoffs: Specialized to fixed-length DNA k-mer keys (not a general-purpose MPHF library); static/immutable once built; relies on PTHash internally so inherits its construction-time/space tradeoffs; needs minimizer sampling tuned per dataset.
caveats: Comparison is against domain-specific k-mer dictionaries (Pufferfish, BLight, dBG-FM), not against std::unordered_map, CMPH, or BBHash directly, so it is only indirect evidence for the MPHF category baseline; numbers are from the peer-reviewed paper (Bioinformatics 2022), not a blog per se, but was surfaced via a k-mer/MPHF blog roundup.
found_via: Blogs / talks: Camille Marchet's 'Minimal Perfect Hash Functions in the k-mer world' blog post (https://kamimrcht.github.io/webpage/mphf.html), which links to SSHash as a genomics MPHF-based dictionary; verified against the SSHash paper and GitHub repo.

verification.tier_reason: This tier covers only the off-category comparison. The peer-reviewed paper (Bioinformatics 38 Suppl. 1, Sec. 5, Tables 3-7) states gcc 11.2.0, -O3 -march=native and an Intel i9-9940X. Only the SSHash side of the harness is public (src/bench.cpp, src/query.cpp, script/benchmark_dictionary.sh at v1.0.0). The Pufferfish, BLight and dBG-FM runs have no published scripts or pinned commits, so the tier is B, not A.
verification.notes: The record's absolute numbers (990/854 ns, 9.39 bpk, 16.2 min, 17.3 GB) all appear in the paper, but they are not wins: SSHash is slower than Pufferfish dense on random lookup. The rejection is on category scope only. SSHash is notable (Bioconda, Rust port) and would qualify under a k-mer-dictionary category. Repo metadata checked: MIT license, not a fork, not archived, 109 stars, last commit 2026-09-03 (active).
verification.reject_reason: other: SSHash is a k-mer dictionary that uses PTHash internally, but every published benchmark compares it only against other k-mer dictionaries. The 2022 paper uses dBG-FM, Pufferfish and BLight. The 2026 paper (btag264) and jermp/kmer_sets_benchmark use SBWT and FMSI. No benchmark compares it against std::unordered_map, CMPH, BBHash or a standalone MPHF, so it does not fit minimal-perfect-hash-functions.

name: BLight
workload: Exact associative index over k-mers of the human genome (k=31): build the index and answer membership/identifier queries over the full reference, using an MPHF (BBHash-style) plus minimizer indexing.
claimed_speedup: Human genome (k=31): 10 min construction / 7.4 GB peak memory / 22.3 bits/k-mer for BLight vs 69 min / 27.4 GB / 55.59 bits/k-mer for Pufferfish; full-reference query time 1,748s single-thread (155s at 12 threads) vs Pufferfish 1,799s single-thread (verbatim from paper Tables 1-2)
hardware: Intel Xeon E5-2420 @ 1.90 GHz, 192 GB RAM, Ubuntu 16.04
tradeoffs: AGPL-3.0 is copyleft and network-use-triggering, a stronger restriction than most catalog entries; specialized to k-mer/genomics keys; static index (no updates) as opposed to Bifrost's dynamic index.
caveats: Compiler/build flags not stated in the paper text I could confirm, so capped at Tier B; only compared against Pufferfish, not std::unordered_map/BBHash/CMPH directly; repo last pushed mid-2024 (stale).
found_via: Blogs / talks: surfaced from the same k-mer/MPHF blog roundup (kamimrcht.github.io/webpage/mphf.html) and cross-checked against the BLight Bioinformatics paper and GitHub repo.

verification.tier_reason: This tier covers only the off-category comparison against Pufferfish. The peer-reviewed paper (Bioinformatics 37(18):2858, Tables 1-2) and the matching bioRxiv v4 preprint name the CPU (Xeon E5-2420) but state no compiler or flags. The repo's bench_blight.cpp times BLight alone, and its makefile uses unversioned g++, so the evidence cannot reach Tier A.
verification.notes: The claimed numbers match the published Tables 1-2. The OUP page came through WebFetch (curl gets 403) and matches bioRxiv 10.1101/546309v4. The rejection is on category scope only. Repo metadata checked: AGPL-3.0, not a fork, not archived, 36 stars, last commit 2024-07-06 (stale).
verification.reject_reason: other: BLight is a k-mer dictionary that uses BBHash internally. Its benchmarks compare it only against the Pufferfish k-mer index (Tables 1-2) and against the Squeakr and SRC abundance indexes, where BLight is slower to build. There is no comparison against std::unordered_map, CMPH, BBHash or a standalone MPHF, so it does not fit minimal-perfect-hash-functions.

name: MQF (Mixed-counters Quotient Filter)
workload: Query time for 35 million existing real k-mers looked up in MQF filters loaded to 60%, 70%, 80% and 90% capacity, with MQF's per-key 'label' feature used as a minimal perfect hash function and compared against BBHash-style MPHFs
claimed_speedup: ~10-fold faster query time than BBHash (MPHFs), with MQF query time reported as invariable across load factors (paper Additional file 1, Figure S6; abstract states "the labels serve as a minimal perfect hash function but are ~10 fold faster than BBhash")
hardware: AWS t3.large instance (2 vCPUs, 8GB RAM), Ubuntu Server 18.04 (exact CPU model not specified; burstable cloud instance type)
stars_or_usage: 12 stars; published in BMC Bioinformatics 22:71 (2021), used in k-mer/genomics counting pipelines from the dib-lab group
tradeoffs: MQF is fundamentally a dynamic counting/labeling quotient filter (supports insert/remove/resize/merge) rather than a pure static MPHF like BBHash, so the 'perfect hash' behavior is one feature (label lookup) of a broader data structure, not a drop-in MPHF replacement; a buffered/disk-backed variant trades speed for memory; comparison hardware is a shared/burstable cloud VM rather than a dedicated bare-metal benchmark box
caveats: Speedup is reported as an aggregate '~10 fold' claim tied to a supplementary figure (Additional file 1, Fig. S6) rather than a detailed per-configuration numeric table; exact CPU model and compiler/optimization flags are not stated, so this is capped at Tier B despite being a peer-reviewed journal paper; the GitHub project has not been updated since October 2023
found_via: WebSearch: 'MQF minimal perfect hash function k-mer "10 fold faster" BBHash github' -> dib-lab/MQF; cross-checked against BMC Bioinformatics paper via PMC (PMC7885209)

verification.tier_reason: The paper (BMC Bioinformatics 22:71) says MQF block labels are ~10x faster than BBHash; Supplementary Fig. S6 shows about 300 ms for MQF vs about 3,100-3,550 ms for BBHash over 35M queries. The only harness for that figure is taggingTest.cpp in dib-lab/2020-paper-mqf-benchmarks (the same file is on the MQF 'benchmark' branch). It builds the MQF through Benchmark_Utils_Script/countingStructure.hpp with qf_init(..., blocksLabelSize=0, ...), so itemOrder() in gqf.cpp returns 0 immediately at `if(qf->metadata->BlockLabel_bits!=32) return 0;` and never searches the filter. That leaves no valid numbers against the baseline.
verification.notes: Category check as requested: MQF is not an MPHF. Its only comparison against a listed baseline for this category is BBHash in Fig. S6, and the published code for that figure never runs the MQF lookup (blocksLabelSize=0 in every version of countingStructure.hpp I checked, back to 2019). I cannot rule out an unpublished local change, but the paper says all experiment code is in that repo. Metadata matches gh: BSD-3-Clause, 12 stars, last commit 2023-10-01, stale.
verification.reject_reason: other: MQF is a counting quotient filter, not an MPHF, and its only comparison against a listed baseline (BBHash, Fig. S6) is invalid because the published harness never performs the MQF lookup
